text:
tara: Heads-up: CI microbench for PR #6612 failed gating. Looks like a perf delta on the batching path, linking the CI output below. Can someone take a look?
perf-bot: [auto] PR 6612 microbench results posted: https://ci.redwood/6612/microbench
perf-bot: ```
TEST: microbatch_latency (baseline v main -> PR)
baseline avg_latency_ms = 12.1
pr avg_latency_ms       = 15.8
delta                   = +30.6% (THRESHOLD +10%)
batcher_queue_wait_ms   = 2.3 -> 5.2 (+126%)
kv_cache_hit_ratio      = 0.84 -> 0.76 (-9.5%)
NOTE: one-off ci noise ok? NO, exceeds gating threshold.
```
frank: Oof. Those queue wait numbers are large. Which microbench exactly?
perf-bot: Test names: microbatch_latency, microbatch_throughput, kv_cache_locality
liam: My immediate suspicion is the kernel selection heuristic tweak from the kernel-selector refactor that landed in PR 6599 — it changed the kernel preference ordering for medium-length sequences. Could change batching and pipeline timing.
frank: Good call. I'll start a quick local perf bisect across main..6612. Running: `./scripts/ci_perf_bisect --test microbatch_latency --range 7a3b2c..HEAD`
jen: FYI 6599 touched autoselect_cost_model + the continuous-batching wait heuristic in scheduler.cpp (small change).
perf-bot: Bisect progress: tested 7a3b2c -> 8f9d1a -> 4c5e6f ... candidate commit identified: `4c5e6f9` (author: liam) — modifies kernel_selector.cc and scheduler.cpp
frank: Local repro confirmed on my devbox with the same microbench. Re-running focused bench:```
commit: 4c5e6f9 (kernel selector reorder)
microbatch_latency: baseline=12.0ms PR=15.6ms (+30%)
batcher_queue_wait_ms: 2.2 -> 5.0
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.85 -> 0.75
```
frank: It looks like the selector change nudged some ops onto a slower kernel variant that increases completion variance, which in turn increases queueing.
liam: That commit also removed an explicit fastpath check for small contiguous KV loads. If true, that could explain the hit ratio drop. I can put together a minimal repro and a proposed patch to restore the check.
jen: Do we want a revert for the rollout-blocking delta, or a targeted fix? This is gating many PRs.
tara: Rollout policy says revert for major regressions that block gating. This is >+10% latency and blocks merges. Let's revert while liam prepares a proper fix.
frank: I'll open a revert PR (6614) now, reverting 4c5e6f9. It will include a note and perf numbers. Linking once created.
perf-bot: [auto] Created perf issue: https://issues.redwood/PR-6612-perf-failure (labels: perf, revert-request)
ci-bot: [CI] Revert PR 6614 running microbench suite...
frank: Revert PR 6614 opened: https://git.redwood/reverts/6614 — please review quick.
liam: ACK, will follow up with a targeted patch that restores the fastpath and refactors kernel ranking to avoid regressions.
jen: Thanks all — please add the microbench case to the perf-regressions watchlist and add the failing traces to the console for later root-cause.
frank: Will attach perf traces and kv histograms to the issue after CI finishes.
ci-bot: [CI] Revert PR 6614 microbench results: avg_latency_ms = 12.2 (baseline), pass gating.
tara: Revert merged, gating unblocked. liam please prioritize the fix and we can re-land with added unit/perf test coverage. :+1:
frank: Got it. I'll close the loop on the issue once the targeted patch is ready.
